passage1.text: Research in human-vehicle interaction has shown even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof.Recent evidence points to drivers'limited understanding ofwhat these systems can and cannot do as a contributing factor to system misuse.A recent study tackles the issue of over-trusting drivers and the resulting system misuse from a legal viewpoint.It looks at what the manufacturers of self-driving cars should legally do to ensure that drivers understand how to use the vehicles appropriately. One solution suggested in the study involves requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements (EULAs), similar to the terms and conditions that require agreement when using new software products.But this is far from ideal.The agreement may not provide enough information to the driver,leading to confusion about the nature of the requests for agreement and their implications.Further,most end users don't read EULAs.A 2017 study shows 91 percent ofpeople agree to them without reading.Among young people,97 percent agree without reviewing the terms. The issue is that,unlike using a smartphone app,operating a car has serious safety risks,whether the driver is human or software.And human drivers need to consent to take responsibility for the outcomes ofthe software and hardware. "Warning fatigue"and distracted driving are also causes for concern.For example,a driver,annoyed after receiving continuous warnings,could decide to just ignore the message.Or,if the message is presented while the vehicle is in motion,it could represent a distraction.Given these limitations and concerns,even if this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward,it likely won't fully protect automakers from their legal liability should the system malfunction(发生故障)or an accident occur. Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations.This needs to occur beyond the vehicle purchase.Recent evidence shows even relying on the information provided by the seller is not going to answer many questions.All ofthis considered,the road forward for self-driving cars is not going to be a smooth ride after all.

passage2.text: Do you ever blend up a protein drink for breakfast,or grab a protein bar following an afternoon workout?If so,you are likely among the millions ofpeople in search ofmore protein-rich diets Protein-enriched products are found everywhere.But contrary to all the publicity that everyone needs more protein,most Americans get twice as much as they need. Many ofus living in the most developed countries are buying into a myth ofprotein deficiency created by food companies and self-identified health experts.Global retail sales ofprotein supplement products reached an astonishing US$18.9 billion in 2020. But are we really in need of more protein?Physicians in the U.S.have never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein. In fact,Americans currently consume almost twice the National Academy ofMedicine's recommended daily intake ofprotein although the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level. For example,if you're a dedicated athlete you might need to consume higher quantities of protein. Generally,though,a 140-pound person should not exceed 120 grams of protein per day,particularly because a high protein diet can strain kidney and liver function and increase risks ofdeveloping heart disease and cancer. While fats and sugar have taken the beating in turns since over a century ago,protein has managed to remain our red-hot favorite. In the 1970s through the 1990s,protein products remained visible but moved back somewhat with the dietary spotlight firmly fixed on low-calorie,low-fat,sugar-free snack foods and beverages following the publication of studies linking sugar and saturated(饱和的)fat consumption to heart disease. 23 ·2024年12月四级真题(第三套) · Later research in 2003,however,suggested high-protein diets could aid in weight loss,and protein quickly regained its former nutrient-superstar status. Now most people living in high-income nations are consuming enough protein.When we replace meals with a protein bar or drink,we also risk missing out on the rich sources of antioxidants(抗氧化剂),vitamins and many other benefits ofreal food.

paragraphs.A: Most people have a dream in life,a vision of who or what they'd like to be in the future.At a minimum, everyone has interests and values that determine what they want out of their lives.Even so,trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging.It can be hard to know where to even begin,and the things you hope to achieve may seem impossible.But,if you're well prepared you may be able to set goals for your life that arejust as fulfilling to work toward as to achieve.
paragraphs.B: We all have goals that we want to achieve in our lives.These goals may include learning a new language eating healthier and losing weight,becoming a better parent,saving more money,and so on.It can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge.This is why we buy courses on how to start a business or how to lose weight fast or how to learn a new language in three months.We assume that ifwe knew about a better strategy,then we would get better results.We believe that a new result requires new knowledge.
paragraphs.C: What I'm starting to realize,however,is that new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results.In fact learning something new can actually be a waste oftime ifyour goal is to make progress and not simply gain additional knowledge.
paragraphs.D: It all comes down to the difference between learning and practicing.Thomas Sterner,in his book The Practicing Mind,explains the key difference between practicing and learning.He says:"When we practice something,we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal.”Here the words “deliberate"and"intention”are key,because they define the difference between actively practicing something and passively learning it.
paragraphs.E: Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar,but these two methods can have profoundly different results.Here are some additional ways to think about the difference.Let's say your goal is to get stronger and more fit.You can research the best instructions on weight lifting technique,but the only way to build strength is to practice lifting weights.Let's say your goal is to grow your startup.You can learn about the best way to make a sales pitch,but the only way to actually land customers is to practice making sales calls.Let's say your goal is to write a book.You can talk to a best-selling author about writing, but the only way to become a better writer is to practice publishing consistently.
paragraphs.F: Passive learning creates knowledge.Active practice creates skill.Let's consider a couple more reasons to prioritize active practice over passive learning.First,passive learning can be a stick that supports inaction. In many cases,learning is actually a way to avoid taking action on the goals and interests that we say are important to us.For example,let's say you want to learn a foreign language.Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly allows you to feel like you are making progress("Hey,I'm figuring out the best way to do this!").Of course,you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language).
paragraphs.G: In situations like this one,we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method,but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels.We make the mistake ofbeing in motion rather than taking action.Learning is valuable until it becomes a form of procrastination (拖延).
paragraphs.H: Another point to consider is that practice is learning,but learning is not practice.Passive learning is not a form of practice because although you gain new knowledge,you are not discovering how to apply that knowledge.Active practice,meanwhile,is one of the greatest forms of learning because the mistakes you make while practicing reveal important insights. D)Even more importantly,practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge. You can watch an online course about how to build a business or read an article about a terrible disaster in a developing nation,but that knowledge is unproductive unless you actually launch your business or donate to those in need.Learning by itself can be valuable for you,but if you want to be valuable to others,then you have to express your knowledge in some way. J)The last important point to consider is that practice focuses your energy on the process.Thomas Sterner once said,"Progress is a natural result of staying focused on the process of doing anything."The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day.When you realize this and begin to direct your focus toward practicing better habits day-in and day-out,continual progress will be the logical outcome.It is not the things we learn nor the dreams we visualize that determine our results,but rather the habits that we practice each day.Fall in love with boredom and focus your energy on the process, not the product. K)What does this all mean?Is passive learning useless?Of course not.In many cases,learning for the sake of learning can be a beautiful thing.Not to mention that soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action.That said,the main point ofthis article is that learning by itself does not lead to progress.We often hide behind information and use learning as an excuse to delay the more difficult and more important choice of actually doing something.Spend less time passively learning and more time actively practicing.Stop thinking and start doing.

questions.script:
Across the U.S., families are looking to the winter with fear as energy costs soar. A number of factors
are creating a bad situation: Global energy consumption is up, but supplies have been reduced. [1] The Energy
Department projects heating bills will jump 28% this winter for those who rely on natural gas. Natural gas is used by
nearly half of U.S. households for heat. Heating oil is projected to be 27% higher and electricity 10% higher. That
comes against inflation rates that accelerated last month with consumer prices growing 6.6%. That's the fastest
pace in four decades.
The pain will be especially acute in parts of the country that heavily rely on heating oil to keep homes warm.
It's projected to cost more than $2,300 to heat a typical home with heating oil this winter. [2] Last month, the federal
government added $1 billion in funding to Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program, bringing the total to $4.8
billion. But that represents a reduction from last year's energy assistance package of over $8 billion.

That's the main finding of a new study by researchers at the U.s. Department of Agriculture in Stoneville, Mississippi.

do. For the study, the researchers asked participants to rate their diet as excellent, very good, good, fair or poor. Folks

M: Well, actually, I've stopped using online payments for the past three months now.

more than what I had budgeted, and by now it's just a habit.

questions.script:
[l6] Lift-off is usually the most environmentally harmful stage of any space mission, with vast quantities of fuel
burnt up in a matter of minutes.For instance, SpaceX's Falcon 9 gets through 112 tonnes of refined fuel, emitting about
336 tonnes of CO2. This is the equivalent produced by your average car driving almost 70 times around the world. [16]
As well as greenhouse gases, rocket engines emit particles that destroy ozone. These issues are growing more pressing
with the emergence of commercial spaceflight. There were 114 space launches in 2020, but there may be up to 1,000
per year in future.
Sustainable fuels are the top priority to enable greener space travel. Current spacecraft use a variety of fuels, but
most are based on fossil fuels. One potentially greener option is liquid hydrogen and oxygen. Hydrogen can be obtained
sustainably by using solar power to break water down into oxygen and hydrogen.
Reusable rockets can cut down on some of the waste associated with spaceflight. [17] Traditionally, boosters, fuel
tanks and other components are treated as expendable. But guiding them back to Earth in a controlled manner opens
new possibilities—most components from the Falcon 9 can be reused up to 100 times.
Truly environmentally friendly space travel is still some way off. [18] But we already have many of the technologies needed to start limiting its impact on our planet.

questions.script:
Helping to look after a pet can facilitate numerous aspects of a child's emotional development. [19] Research
shows that reading to a loyal and nonjudgmental companion, such as a dog or cat, can encourage reluctant readers to
read aloud, which will in turn boost their self-confidence. Having a companion to talk to about their feelings can also
help children feel secure and develop communication skills.
A household pet can also cultivate a child's sense of responsibility as their parent explains the necessary processes
of keeping their pet happy and healthy. As a child matures, they can then take on more of the daily responsibilities,
boosting their sense of independence.
[20] Pets also provide a fantastic subject for research and learning. Parents can encourage their child to research
their favourite pets at the library or during a supervised internet search. Taking children along to the pet shop to buy
food and supplies will support their cognitive development as their passion for learning flourishes.
A child's physical development can benefit greatly from taking pets for walks in the fresh air. Even their fine-
motor skills can be utilised in taking care of a beloved animal.
When responsibilities are well paced and communicated, a child can benefit greatly from involvement in bringing
up a happy and healthy pet. [2i] And of course, if a child doesn't have a pet in their own household, they can still
benefit from all of the above when visiting a friend who does.

students a packet of information. This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships. It would also include
expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill. He said it would give

colleges out of state. [25] Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.

require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.

options.D: Some students may lack adequate access. Part Ⅲ Reading Comprehension (40 minutes)

questions.script:
[22] A new bill in the Ohio legislature would require state public colleges and universities to send prospective
students a packet of information. This would include costs of college, grants and scholarships. It would also include
expected monthly loan payments and projected salary after college.
State Representative Adam Mathews is one of the two legislators who proposed the bill. He said it would give
prospective students more information about what to expect once they graduate."Putting that information in front of
them will give them the best opportunity to match their skills and their dreams to what our schools can provide, said
Mathews. [23] He notes that the state can only regulate public institutions in this way, but he hopes private institutions
in Ohio follow the lead of the state and post similar information. He believes giving out this information will help
Ohio's colleges and universities to be more competitive. The information will highlight what a great value they have for
their very reasonable cost.
[24] Ohio's schools are already competitive. The state attracts more undergraduate students than it sends to
colleges out of state. [25] Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites.
This includes tuition, fees, graduation rates and more, But students need to search for the information. This bill would
require the universities and colleges to send a packet directly to students.
questions.expl: 原文提到“Many colleges and universities currently provide similar information on their websites... But students need to search for the information”，即问题是“学生必须自行查找信息”。选项A“浪费时间上网”、B“访问太多网站”、D“缺乏访问权限”均未提及。 涉及知识点：听力短文转折关系捕捉（but 引出问题核心）、同义替换（have to search for the information 对应 need to search for the information）

questions.stem: 第 26 空
questions.expl: normal 详解： 语法判断：空格前为不定冠词a，后为名词face，需填入形容词或分词修饰face。 语义判断：上下文对比“真实面孔”与“戴面具的人”，此处指参与者判断照片中哪些是“正常的面孔”，normal（正常的）符合语境，与“wearing a mask”形成逻辑对比。 涉及知识点：形容词修饰名词的语法结构、语境逻辑对比分析。

questions.stem: 第 27 空
questions.expl: observed 详解： 语法判断：空格处需填入分词，作The 20% error rate的后置定语，补充说明该错误率的来源。 语义判断：前文提及研究过程与结果，该错误率是通过实验“观察到”的客观数据，observed（观察到的）符合语境，排除主观类词汇。 涉及知识点：分词作后置定语的语法结构、实验类语境词汇辨析。

questions.stem: 第 28 空
questions.expl: 详解： 语法判断：空格前为不定冠词an，后为名词face，需填入以元音音素开头的形容词或分词。 语义判断：上下文围绕“区分真假面孔”展开，此处指“人造面孔”（与real thing对应），artificial（人造的、假的）符合语境，且以元音音素开头，匹配an的用法。 涉及知识点：不定冠词an的用法（后接元音音素开头的单词）、反义词对应（artificial vs real）。

questions.stem: 第 29 空
questions.expl: establish 详解： 语法判断：空格前为不定式符号to，后为宾语any differences，需填入动词原形。 语义判断：研究收集不同种族参与者的数据，目的是“确定”种族差异，establish（确定、证实）符合实验研究的语境，搭配differences合理。 涉及知识点：不定式作目的状语、实验类动词搭配（establish differences）。

questions.stem: 第 30 空
questions.expl: accurate 详解： 语法判断：空格处与slower构成并列比较结构（response times were slower and selections were 5% less...），需填入形容词。 语义判断：前文提及区分真假面孔存在困难，面对不同种族面孔时，反应时间变慢，“准确性”下降，accurate（准确的）符合逻辑，less accurate对应“准确性降低”。 涉及知识点：并列比较结构、形容词比较级的隐含表达（less + 形容词原级）。

questions.stem: 第 31 空
questions.expl: passed 详解： 语法判断：空格前为助动词have，后为反身代词themselves及介词off，需填入过去分词，构成现在完成时，且需符合“pass oneself off as”的固定搭配。 语义判断：语境为刑事案件中罪犯“冒充”他人，pass oneself off as是固定短语，意为“冒充、假冒”，符合“误导警方调查”的逻辑。 涉及知识点：现在完成时的构成（have + 过去分词）、固定短语搭配（pass oneself off as）。

questions.stem: 第 32 空
questions.expl: extremely 详解： 语法判断：空格后为形容词realistic，需填入副词修饰该形容词。 语义判断：案例中犯罪团伙冒充法国部长并骗取巨款，说明面具“极其”逼真，extremely（极度、极其）程度强烈，符合语境，突出面具的高仿真性。 涉及知识点：副词修饰形容词的语法结构、程度副词的语义辨析。

questions.stem: 第 33 空
questions.expl: cheating 详解： 语法判断：空格前为主句（an international gang used an extremely realistic mask...），需填入非谓语动词，且符合“cheat sb. out of sth.”的固定搭配。 语义判断：语境为“骗取企业高管数百万英镑”，cheat sb. out of sth.是固定短语，意为“骗取某人某物”，cheating在此处作现在分词，表结果状语，符合逻辑。 涉及知识点：非谓语动词（现在分词作结果状语）、固定短语搭配（cheat sb. out of sth.）。

questions.stem: 第 34 空
questions.expl: allow 详解： 语法判断：空格前为情态动词may，后为名词短语the key characteristics，需填入动词原形，且符合“allow sth. to be done”的固定结构。 语义判断：语境为超逼真面具“使”人脸关键特征被错误识别，allow（使能够、允许）符合“allow the key characteristics...to be identified”的结构，表达“使某事发生”的含义。 涉及知识点：情态动词后接动词原形、固定结构（allow sth. to be done）。

questions.stem: 第 35 空
questions.expl: 详解： 语法判断：空格前为be动词，后为过去分词identified，需填入副词修饰该分词。 语义判断：前文提及无法识别合成人脸会影响安全，此处指“错误地”识别关键特征，incorrectly（错误地）符合语境，与前文“错误判断”“误导调查”形成呼应。 涉及知识点：副词修饰过去分词的语法结构、语义逻辑呼应（incorrectly与前文error rate对应）。

questions.stem: 36. Acquisition ofnew knowledge may not guarantee the progress that you aim to make.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“new knowledge”“may not guarantee the progress”，对应C段首句“new knowledge does not necessarily drive new results”及下文“if your goal is to make progress... learning something new can actually be a waste of time”。 语义解析：题干“获得新知识可能并不能保证你想要取得的进步”是对C段核心观点的同义转述，其中“may not guarantee the progress”对应“does not necessarily drive new results”，“you aim to make”对应“your goal is to make progress”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义转述识别（does not necessarily = may not; drive new results = guarantee the progress）。

questions.stem: 37. Your current situation in life is built on the beliefs and habits you have been practicing daily.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“current situation in life”“the beliefs and habits you have been practicing daily”，对应J段第三句“The state of your life right now is a result of the habits and beliefs that you have been practicing each day”。 语义解析：题干是对原文句子的同义转述，“current situation in life”对应“The state of your life right now”，“is built on”对应“is a result of”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义替换（current situation = state of life; built on = result of）。

questions.stem: 38. Knowing the best way to learn a foreign language will not enable you to speak it without actual practice.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“the best way to learn a foreign language”“speak it without actual practice”，对应F段例子“Reading a book on how to learn a foreign language quickly... you're not actually practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language)”。 语义解析：题干概括了F段例子的核心逻辑——仅知道学习外语的方法，没有实际练习无法学会说外语，“Knowing the best way”对应“figuring out the best way”，“will not enable you to speak it without actual practice”对应“not practicing the action that would deliver your desired outcome (speaking the foreign language)”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、例子与主旨的对应关系、同义转述。

questions.stem: 39. People may find it demanding to create a goal which will take a long time to achieve.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“demanding”“create a goal which will take a long time to achieve”，对应A段第三句“trying to set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years can be extremely challenging”。 语义解析：题干是对原文的同义转述，“create a goal which will take a long time to achieve”对应“set achievable goals that you'll work for over the course of many years”，“may find it demanding”对应“can be extremely challenging”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义替换（demanding = challenging; create a goal = set goals; take a long time = over the course of many years）。

questions.stem: 40. Learning and practicing seem to be very much alike,but the two processes can lead to quite different outcomes.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“Learning and practicing”“very much alike”“quite different outcomes”，对应E段第一句“Learning something new and practicing something new may seem very similar, but these two methods can have profoundly different results”。 语义解析：题干与原文核心内容一致，“seem to be very much alike”对应“may seem very similar”，“quite different outcomes”对应“profoundly different results”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义替换（alike = similar; outcomes = results）。

questions.stem: 41. Absorbing new information is helpful in making better decisions prior to action.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“Absorbing new information”“helpful in making better decisions prior to action”，对应K段第五句“soaking up new information can help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action”。 语义解析：题干是对原文的同义转述，“Absorbing new information”对应“soaking up new information”，“helpful in making better decisions prior to action”对应“help you make more informed decisions when you do decide to take action”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义替换（absorb = soak up; better decisions = more informed decisions; prior to action = when you do decide to take action）。

questions.stem: 42. Sometimes we may feel like we are making progress by doing some research or making preparations,but actually we are staying at the starting point.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“making progress by doing some research or making preparations”“staying at the starting point”，对应G段第一句“we often claim that we are preparing or researching the best method, but these rationalizations allow us to feel like we are moving forward when we are merely spinning our wheels”。 语义解析：题干概括了原文逻辑，“feel like we are making progress by doing some research or making preparations”对应“feel like we are moving forward”，“staying at the starting point”对应“merely spinning our wheels”（白费力气）。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、习语理解（spin one's wheels = 白费力气）、同义转述。

questions.stem: 43. We are inclined to think that a lack ofknowledge prevents us from advancing to a better future.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“a lack of knowledge”“prevents us from advancing to a better future”，对应B段第三句“it can be easy to assume that the gap between where you are now and where you want to be in the future is caused by a lack of knowledge”。 语义解析：题干是对原文的深层理解，原文“现在与未来的差距由知识匮乏造成”即“知识匮乏阻碍走向更美好未来”，“are inclined to think”对应“can be easy to assume”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、语义深层转换（gap caused by lack of knowledge = lack of knowledge prevents advancing）。

questions.stem: 44. Learning can benefit you by itself,but only practice can turn what you learn into meaningful contributions.
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“Learning can benefit you by itself”“practice”“meaningful contributions”，对应I段首句“practice is the only way to make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge”及尾句“Learning by itself can be valuable for you, but if you want to be valuable to others, then you have to express your knowledge in some way”。 语义解析：题干概括了I段核心观点——学习本身有价值，但只有实践能将知识转化为有意义的贡献，“turn what you learn into meaningful contributions”对应“make a meaningful contribution with your knowledge”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、段落主旨概括、同义转述。

questions.stem: 45. Practice involves repeating a process intentionally to attain a
questions.expl: 题干定位：题干关键信息“Practice”“repeating a process intentionally”“attain a particular objective”，对应D段第三句“when we practice something, we are involved in the deliberate repetition of a process with the intention of reaching a specific goal”。 语义解析：题干是对原文引用句的同义转述，“involves repeating a process intentionally”对应“involved in the deliberate repetition of a process”，“attain a particular objective”对应“reaching a specific goal”。 涉及知识点：信息匹配技巧、同义替换（intentionally = deliberate; attain = reach; objective = goal）。

questions.stem: 46. What do we learn from research in human-vehicle interaction?

options.A: Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors.
options.B: Driverless vehicles are likely to be misused by some people.
options.C: Self-driving car manufacturers are not aware ofthe legal matters involved.
options.D: There is a long way to go before humans can interact with driverless vehicles

questions.expl: Automatic driving systems are by no means immune to errors. 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“research in human-vehicle interaction”定位到第一段第一句。 解析：原文指出“even systems designed to automate driving are far from being error-proof”，“far from being error-proof”意为“远不能避免出错”，与选项A“by no means immune to errors”（绝非不会出错）同义，故A正确。 排除干扰项： B项：原文提到“system misuse”，但未说“无人驾驶汽车很可能被误用”，无依据； C项：原文提到研究“从法律角度探讨制造商应采取的措施”，但未说“制造商未意识到法律问题”，无依据； D项：文章基于“人车已能交互”展开讨论，“还有很长路要走”与原文不符。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、同义替换（far from error-proof = by no means immune to errors）。

questions.stem: 47. What is the problem with requiring buyers to sign end-user license agreements?

options.A: End users,young and old alike,find the terms complex to interpret.
options.B: Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms.
options.C: Many people are often confused by the wording ofthe terms.
options.D: Most end users do not understand the terms after reading them through.

questions.expl: Most end users sign them without bothering to read the terms. 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“sign end-user license agreements”定位到第二段。 解析：原文明确提到“most end users don't read EULAs. A 2017 study shows 91 percent of people agree to them without reading. Among young people, 97 percent agree without reviewing the terms”，与选项B“大多数终端用户都懒得阅读条款就签署了协议”完全一致，故B正确。 排除干扰项：A、C、D三项均未在原文提及“条款复杂”“措辞困惑”“阅读后不理解”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、直接信息对应。

questions.stem: 48. What would drivers do when they suffer from"warning fatigue"?

options.A: Waste no time keeping the car moving.
options.B: Rest a while to avoid fatigue driving.
options.C: Take no action despite repeated warnings.
options.D: Take note ofthe message though fatigued.

questions.expl: Take no action despite repeated warnings. 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“warning fatigue”定位到第四段第二句。 解析：原文举例说明“驾驶员在连续收到警告后会感到恼火，可能会选择直接忽视该信息”，“忽视信息”即“尽管反复收到警告，仍不采取任何行动”，与选项C一致，故C正确。 排除干扰项：A、B、D三项均未在原文提及“继续行驶”“休息”“留意信息”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、例子与主旨的对应关系。

questions.stem: 49. What does the author think ofcontinuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements?

options.A: It will probably not guarantee the safety of drivers in case of accidents.
options.B: It likely won't ensure that the automatic driving system functions properly.
options.C: It likely won't fully protect automakers against accusations of deliberate cheating.
options.D: It will probably not provide manufacturers adequate protection from legal responsibilities.

questions.expl: 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“continuing to ask buyers to sign end-user license agreements”定位到第四段最后一句（题干中“continuing to ask...”对应原文“this mode of obtaining consent is to move forward”）。 解析：原文指出“即使这种获取同意的模式得以推进，也可能无法充分保护汽车制造商在系统出现故障或发生事故时免于承担法律责任”，与选项D“无法为制造商提供足够多免除法律责任的保护”同义，故D正确。 排除干扰项： A项：原文聚焦“保护制造商”，而非“保证驾驶员安全”，偏离核心； B项：原文未提及“保证系统正常运行”，无依据； C项：原文未提及“故意欺诈的指控”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、同义替换（fully protect... from legal liability = provide adequate protection from legal responsibilities）。

questions.stem: 50. What should be done to help drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations?

options.A: Training them to be experts in vehicle automation.
options.B: Familiarizing them with the systems through training.
options.C: Broadening their knowledge of accident-prevention mechanisms.
options.D: Facilitating their access to the information provided by the seller.

questions.expl: 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“fully understand system capabilities and limitations”定位到最后一段第一句。 解析：原文明确提到“Driver training for self-driving vehicles can help ensure that drivers fully understand system capabilities and limitations”，即“通过培训让驾驶员熟悉系统”，与选项B一致，故B正确。 排除干扰项： A项：原文未提及“培训成为专家”，过度延伸； C项：原文未提及“事故预防机制”，无依据； D项：原文提到“依靠卖方提供的信息无法回答许多问题”，故“获取卖方信息”不可行，排除。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、直接信息对应。

questions.stem: 51. What do we learn about publicity over protein in America?

options.A: It has helped to create the myth ofprotein deficiency.
options.B: It has helped Americans in search ofprotein-rich diets.
options.C: It has raised a lot ofhealth concerns among the public.
options.D: It has been funded by food companies and health experts.

questions.expl: 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“publicity over protein in America”定位到第二段和第三段。 解析：第二段提到“与每个人都需要更多蛋白质的宣传相反，大多数美国人摄入的蛋白质是所需量的两倍”，第三段进一步指出“这种宣传让人们相信了食品公司和自诩健康专家创造的蛋白质缺乏的错误观念”，即宣传助长了“蛋白质缺乏”的神话，与选项A一致，故A正确。 排除干扰项： B项：原文未说宣传“帮助美国人寻找富含蛋白质的饮食”，而是指出宣传造成误导，无依据； C项：原文未提及宣传“引起健康担忧”，无依据； D项：原文未提及宣传“得到资助”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、段落逻辑衔接分析。

questions.stem: 52. Why have physicians in the U.S.never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency?

options.A: Americans can purchase many kinds of protein-rich foods everywhere.
options.B: Americans can absorb the number of calories recommended by food experts.
options.C: Americans can get sufficient proteinjust by eating adequate foods daily.
options.D: Americans can rely on food supplements to prevent protein deficiency

questions.expl: 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“physicians in the U.S. never actually examined a patient with protein deficiency”定位到第四段第二句。 解析：原文明确给出原因“because simply by eating an adequate number of daily calories we are also most likely getting enough protein”，即“每天摄入足够的热量（即吃足够的食物）就会获得足够的蛋白质”，与选项C一致，故C正确。 排除干扰项： A项：原文未说“通过购买富含蛋白质的食品”获取，而是正常饮食，排除； B项：原文是“摄入足够的热量”，而非“专家建议的热量”，偷换概念； D项：原文未提及“依赖食品补充剂”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、因果关系对应。

questions.stem: 53. What should people take into consideration in deciding on the most preferable protein intake?

options.A: How healthy they are and what food they eat.
options.B: How old they are and what activities they do.
options.C: How much protein they consume and what their body weight is.
options.D: How serious their protein deficiency is and what remedies they use.

questions.expl: 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“the most preferable protein intake”定位到第五段（题干中“preferable”对应原文“desirable”）。 解析：原文提到“the most desirable protein intake may vary depending on age and activity level”，即“最理想的蛋白质摄入量因年龄和活动水平而异”，“activity level”对应“what activities they do”，与选项B一致，故B正确。 排除干扰项：A、C、D三项提及的“健康状况”“食物类型”“体重”“缺乏程度”等均未在原文提及，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、同义替换（activity level = what activities they do）。

questions.stem: 54. What foods have been largely out of favor for more than a century?

questions.expl: Sugary and fatty foods. 详解： 定位：根据题干关键词“more than a century”“largely out of favor”定位到第七段（题干中“out of favor”对应原文“take the beating”，“more than a century”对应原文“over a century”）。 解析：原文指出“一个多世纪以来，脂肪和糖一直轮流受到攻击，而蛋白质却一直是我们的最爱”，“受到攻击”即“不受欢迎”，脂肪和糖对应“含糖和高脂肪的食物”，与选项D一致，故D正确。 排除干扰项： A项：原文提到“低热量、低脂肪、无糖零食”曾是焦点，并非不受欢迎； B项：蛋白质一直是最爱，并非不受欢迎； C项：原文未提及“红肉和白肉”，无依据。 涉及知识点：细节理解题、习语理解（take the beating = 不受欢迎、受攻击）。
